claim.summary: For a finite multiset of complex points other than 0 and 1, closed under conjugation and rho -> 1 - conj(rho), with lambda_n = sum m(1 - (1 - 1/rho)^n): lambda_n = S_on(n) + sum over off-line pairs of m(2 - (r^n + r^-n) cos n phi) with S_on >= 0; with tau = delta/(min(beta, 1-beta)^2 + gamma^2), lambda_n >= S_on(n) - 4 sum m sinh^2(n tau/2), so for n <= 1/tau_max the off-line pairs lower lambda_n by less than 1.09 each and lambda_n < 0 forces n tau_max > log(S_on(n)/M_off); and any off-line point makes lambda_n negative for infinitely many n.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof (partner pairs have reciprocal-conjugate w; Dirichlet simultaneous approximation for the last part). Finite model of Li's criterion with the index threshold of order gamma^2/delta for a pair at height gamma and distance delta. Nothing is derived about the coefficients of zeta; the criterion's sources are not read.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Locates the index range in which Li's positivity could detect an off-line zero at a given height: of order height squared over distance.
significance.next_action: Read a source for the arithmetic formula of the coefficients and for what is known unconditionally at large index.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry; no computation.

significance.note: Context: the last part is the finite model of a known criterion; the threshold form is elementary. Novelty not claimed.

relationships.note: Analogous to the pair atom's exponential weight in the Gram model, with n/gamma^2 in the place of the bandwidth.

claim.summary: For real even phi in L^2 supported in [-Lam/2,Lam/2], grid step 2pi/Lam over Z and v_z=(phihat(z-alpha_k))_k: v_z^T v_w = Lam (phi^2)^(z-w), v_z^* v_w = Lam (phi^2)^(w-conj z); a conjugate pair z, conj z off the real axis at distance delta has normalized atom (kappa+1) e_x e_x^T - (kappa-1) e_y e_y^T with kappa = int phi^2 cosh(2 delta u) / int phi^2 > 1.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof by Parseval on the interval and evenness. The bilinear identity is the imported density proof's Poisson identity; the Hermitian companion at complex arguments and the two-eigenvalue form are worked out here. Abstract complete-grid statement; says nothing about actual zeta zeros.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: Elementary consequence of Fourier-series orthogonality, expected to be known in the explicit-formula literature; recorded as the model for the bridge test, no novelty claimed.
significance.next_action: Use for the many-pair cancellation computation; before applying to the imported cut form verify the tail hypothesis for its smoothed window.

mathematical_status.note: Complete proof in the entry for every bandwidth and every real even L^2 window supported in the interval; numerical control on four parameter pairs agrees.

significance.note: Context-level elementary lemma; novelty not claimed and not searched in the literature.

relationships.note: Extends the Poisson identity used in the imported density deduction to Hermitian products at complex arguments. Second moment of the complete-grid Gram form with several off-line pairs: new relationship with lem:gram-second-moment-identity, prop:many-pair-norm-bound. Extreme eigenvalues of the complete-grid Gram form with one off-line pair: new relationship with prop:extreme-eigenvalue-detection. Li's coefficients of a finite configuration with off-line pairs: new relationship with prop:li-coefficient-threshold.

relationships.scope: The pair's weight exp(n delta/gamma^2) is the analogue of kappa at bandwidth n/gamma^2; an analogy, no estimate transferred.
